entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Cleobulus of Lindos was a Greek poet and a native of the island city of Lindos in ancient Greece. He is one of the Seven Sages of Greece, a group of seven wise men who were revered for their wisdom and philosophical insights.

As a member of this influential group, Cleobulus played a significant role in shaping the intellectual and cultural landscape of ancient Greece. He was known for his poetic compositions, which often explored themes of love, beauty, and the human condition. His works have been preserved through the centuries and continue to be studied by scholars today.

Cleobulus' significance extends beyond his literary contributions, as he also played a role in the political and philosophical debates of ancient Greece. As a Sage, he was sought out for his counsel on matters of state and morality, and his writings reflect a deep understanding of the complexities of human nature.

One of Cleobulus' most lasting legacies is his influence on Western philosophy and literature. His poetic compositions have been cited as an inspiration by later writers such as Plato and Aristotle, who were deeply influenced by his ideas on beauty, love, and the human condition.

In conclusion, Cleobulus of Lindos was a significant figure in ancient Greek intellectual history, whose contributions to poetry, philosophy, and politics continue to be felt today.
